+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: Declare the acp-client executable target, product and dependencies
+---
+## What
+
+`cli-plan.md` §3 and §4 add one executable to this package. This task makes it
+build and makes it reachable from an other package.
+
+Edit `Package.swift`:
+
+- Add two dependencies. `apple/swift-argument-parser`, `from: "1.8.0"`, the same
+  floor `FoundationModelsExtras` uses, so the checkout is shared. And
+  `tuist/Noora`, the terminal design system §5 selects. Resolve Noora, read the
+  version SwiftPM picks, and pin that version as the `from:` floor. Write a
+  comment on each new dependency that gives its reason, matching the style of
+  the comments already in the file.
+- Add `.executable(name: "acp-client", targets: ["acp-client"])` to `products`.
+  It must be a product, and not a target alone: `FoundationModelsACPAgent` will
+  depend on this package and spawn this binary from its own tests (§17).
+- Add `.executableTarget(name: "acp-client", ...)` at path
+  `Sources/acp-client/`. Its dependencies are exactly four: the
+  `FoundationModelsACPClient` target, the `FoundationModelsACP` product, the
+  `ArgumentParser` product, and the `Noora` product. §12 permits no more.
+- Add the target `"acp-client"` to the dependencies of the
+  `FoundationModelsACPClientTests` test target, so the unit suite can
+  `import acp_client`.
+
+Create `Sources/acp-client/AcpClient.swift`. The file must NOT be named
+`main.swift`: a target with top-level code cannot be imported by a test target.
+Declare `@main struct AcpClient: AsyncParsableCommand` with a
+`configuration` that names the command `acp-client` and gives its abstract. The
+subcommand tree belongs to the next task; this task needs only a version string
+and a body that builds.
+
+Put the version in one place: `Sources/acp-client/AcpClientVersion.swift`, a
+`public enum AcpClientVersion { public static let current = "0.1.0" }`, so
+`--version` and the tests read the same constant.
+
+`Tests/FoundationModelsACPClientTests/ForbiddenImportTests.swift` already scans
+every Swift file below `Sources/`, so it now covers the executable too. Update
+its doc comment to say so. Do not change the forbidden list: §12 bans the same
+modules from the binary that `plan.md` bans from the library.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] `swift build` builds the `acp-client` target.
+- [ ] `swift build --product acp-client` produces a runnable binary.
+- [ ] `Package.swift` declares the `acp-client` executable product.
+- [ ] The `acp-client` target declares exactly four dependencies, and none of
+      them is `FoundationModels`, `FoundationModelsACPAgent`,
+      `FoundationModelsMCP`, `FoundationModelsRouter` or `SwiftUI`.
+- [ ] The unit test target can `import acp_client`.
+- [ ] `Package.resolved` holds `swift-argument-parser` and `Noora` at the pinned
+      versions.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] New `Tests/FoundationModelsACPClientTests/ManifestTests.swift`. It reads
+      `Package.swift` through the existing `RepositoryFile.read(relativePath:)`
+      helper and asserts: the file declares
+      `.executable(name: "acp-client"`; the `acp-client` target block names
+      `ArgumentParser` and `Noora`; and the block names none of the five
+      forbidden modules. The test protects the product declaration that the
+      agent package depends on.
+- [ ] New `Tests/FoundationModelsACPClientTests/AcpClientVersionTests.swift`.
+      It `import acp_client` and asserts `AcpClientVersion.current` is a
+      non-empty string of three dot-separated numbers. This test also proves
+      the executable target is importable, which every later CLI unit test
+      needs.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPClientTests/ForbiddenImportTests.swift` still
+      passes with the new source directory in the scan.
+- [ ] Run `swift test` and `swift build --product acp-client`. Both succeed.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
